intelligence.enrichment: Floating and sinking must be reasoned from material properties rather than size alone; the chapter uses density-related examples such as ice being lighter than liquid water and bamboo being light and hollow, while noting that density is not the only factor deciding whether something floats or sinks. Differences in material properties such as density can make same-sized objects feel differently heavy and can help explain why some objects float while others sink. The learner correctly applies this rule: Floating and sinking must be reasoned from material properties rather than size alone; the chapter uses density-related examples such as ice being lighter than liquid water and bamboo being light and hollow, while noting that density is not the only factor deciding whether something floats or sinks. Small or light-looking objects float and big or heavy-looking objects sink.
